deep.reconstruction:
Context: Gauss's ephemeris reduction of Pallas for its tenth opposition in 1814. The following page applies these constants to his own observation of 16 Sept. and to Bessel's Königsberg observations. The page has five steps.

(1) EPOCH AND PRECESSION. 1814 Oct 25.52143 = 1810 Jan 0 + 1759.52317 d = 1803 Jan 0 + 4316.52317 d.
- Calendar check (mine): 1810–1813 contain 1461 d, plus 298 d to Oct 25 gives 1759. Also 1803–1809 contain 2557 d, and 2557 + 1759 = 4316.
- The 0.00174 d offset between .52143 and .52317 is presumably a meridian or time-reckoning difference; this is unexplained on the page.
- Precession: log 1759.52317 = 3.24540. The daily rate has log 9.13725, i.e. 0.13718"/d. Sum 2.38265, so the general precession is 241.35".

(2) INTERPOLATION OF PERTURBATIONS. The perturbations di, dΩ, 50·dμ, dφ, dω, dε are tabulated at t = 4256, 4306, 4356 (step 50 d) and interpolated to t = 4316.523 (n = 0.2105) by second-order (Stirling/Bessel-type) interpolation. Results:
- di = −143.66"
- dΩ = −257.77"
- 50dμ = −111.71665", so dμ = −2.234333"
- dφ = −875.62"
- dω = −495.30"
- dε = −384.993"

A last column at 4281, 4331, 4381 has first differences equal to the 50dμ values, i.e. it is the summed (integrated) mean-motion perturbation. Interpolated it gives −5498.27".

The osculating/perturbed elements then follow:
- i = 34°35'18.03" (confirmed by the later half-sum computation).
- Ω = Ω0 − 257.77" + 241.35" (precession) − 18.10" (nutation) = 172°33'35.22".
- π = π0 − 495.30" + 241.35" − 18.10" = 121°8'45.89".
- φ = 13°58'8.40" (e = sin φ ≈ 0.2414).
- Mean motion n = 770.71831" − 2.234333" = 768.48398"/d, which is sidereal; the tropical value is 768.62114" (= +0.13716).
- log a = 0.4429145, from Kepler's third law: a = (k/n)^(2/3) with k = 3548.18761".
- Mean-motion part of the longitude: 1759.52317 × 770.71831 = 1356096.72" = 376°41'36.72".

(3) TRANSFORMATION OF THE ORBIT TO THE EQUATOR. Gauss solves the spherical triangle formed by equator, ecliptic and orbit with his analogies (Gauss/Delambre analogies). Inputs:
- obliquity ε = 23°27'46.82" (apparent)
- (ε − i)/2 = −5°33'45.605"
- (ε + i)/2 = 29°1'32.425"
- Ω/2 = 86°16'47.61"

The logs of the sines and cosines of these are combined to get the half-sum (δ' + Δ)/2 = 86°43'50.49" and half-difference (δ' − Δ)/2 = 288°1'39.40" (= −71°58'20.60"). Hence:
- right ascension of the equatorial node δ' = 158°42'11.09"
- arc between the nodes Δ = 14°45'29.89"
- inclination to the equator i' with log cos i' = 9.9909177 and log sin i' = 9.3061950 (i' ≈ 11.68°).

The argument of perihelion from the ecliptic node is π − Ω = 308°35'10.67". Adding Δ gives the argument of perihelion from the equatorial node: ω' = 323°20'40.56".

Gaussian equatorial constants, so that (x, y, z) = r·(sin a·sin(A+u), sin b·sin(B+u), sin c·sin(C+u)):
- sin a·sin A = cos δ'
- sin a·cos A = −sin δ'·cos i'
- sin b·sin B = sin δ'
- sin b·cos B = cos δ'·cos i'
- sin c = sin i', C = 0

This yields:
- A = 249°6'19.57", log sin a = 9.9988234
- B = 158°17'40.15", log sin b = 9.9921378
- log sin c = 9.3061950

With u = v + ω', the arguments are A + ω' = 212°27'0.13", B + ω' = 121°38'20.71", C + ω' = 323°20'40.56".

(4) ECCENTRIC-ANOMALY FORM. Substituting r·cos v = a(cos E − e) and r·sin v = b·sin E (log b = log a + log cos φ = 0.4298771) gives r·sin(v + A') = a·sinA'·cos E + b·cosA'·sin E − a·e·sinA'. Gauss tabulates:
- log a·sin a = 0.4417379 and log b·sin a = 0.4287005, etc.
- products such as 0.1713594n, 0.3549707n, 0.3651703, 0.1418157n, 9.5250844n, 9.6403767
- log(−e) = 9.3827317n

Each pair P·cos E + Q·sin E is reduced to K·sin(E + M) (auxiliary log cos 9.9224358 etc.). Results:
- x = 10^0.4325349 · sin(E + 213°14'1.37") + 0.3581716
- y = 10^0.4315421 · sin(E + 120°52'34.25") − 0.5596313
- z = 10^9.7408084 · sin(E + 322°31'2.57") + 0.0808753

(5) MEAN ANOMALIES FOR BESSEL'S KÖNIGSBERG OBSERVATIONS. The epoch mean anomaly at Oct 25.0 was inferred from the observations of Oct 21 (302°56'6.54") and Oct 28 (302°56'4.61"); their mean, 302°56'5.57", is adopted.

Königsberg observation times are given in hours and decimal minutes, with the light-time (aberration) column 14'2.3" … 13'48.8":
- 12h31.255m = 12.52092h, giving Oct 14.52170
- the other times are converted the same way, up to Oct 35.45394 (= Nov 4)

For each observation, log|t − Oct 25.0| is added to log 768.62114 = 2.8857123, giving nΔt (e.g. 8053.84", 7287.60", …). The mean anomaly is M = 302°56'5.57" ∓ nΔt, e.g. 300°41'51.73" … 305°10'0.69". The eccentric anomaly E is obtained from Kepler's equation M = E − e·sin E (e in arc ≈ 13.831°), e.g. 287°30'26.48" … 292°22'38.49". These E values feed the x, y, z formulas of step 4.
errors: The nΔt for Oct 14.52170 must be 8053.84" (10^(1.0202906+2.8857123)). The subtraction 302°56'5.57" − 8053.84" = 300°41'51.73" confirms Gauss used 8053.84; the transcription '8053.24' is a misreading of an overwritten digit.
dφ interpolates to −875.65" by second-order interpolation, against Gauss's −875.62". The 0.03" discrepancy is negligible; it is possibly a slight slip or a different interpolation formula.
Ω is written 172.33.35.32 at the top but 172.33.35,22 below. The halving 86°16'47.61" uses 35.22, so the top value is a 0.1" slip or a misreading.
Inclination appears as 34.37.18.03 in the upper block but 34.35.18.03 in the triangle computation. (ε − i)/2 = −5°33'45.605" confirms 34°35'18.03".

Possible conceptual slip, flagged as uncertain: the mean anomaly is advanced with the tropical motion 768.62114"/d rather than the sidereal/anomalistic 768.48398"/d. The difference is about 0.137"/d, i.e. ≤1.5" over the 10-day span. It may be deliberate within Gauss's reference-frame conventions.
The difference between epochs Oct 25.52143 and 25.52317 (0.00174 d), and between these and the anomaly epoch Oct 25.0, is not explained on the page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine, though careful, ephemeris computation within Gauss's well-known Pallas perturbation program (1810s). It uses methods he himself published in Theoria Motus. There is no new mathematics; its value is as an archival record of his working data for the 1814 opposition.

transcription_corrections: '8053.24' should read 8053.84 (an 8 written over a digit).
'34.37.18.03' (top) should be 34.35.18.03, as in the triangle block.
'π−δ' = 308.35.10,67' should be π−Ω = 308.35.10.67 (perihelion minus ecliptic node).
Königsberg times are in hours and decimal minutes: '12h 31'255' = 12h 31.255m, '26,783' = 26.783m, etc. They are not seconds.
'2,8857123' is log of the tropical mean motion 768.62114 and heads the log Δt column. The column of logs is log|t − Oct 25.0|.
'Für die Epoche der Mit[?]' is probably 'Mittl. Anomalie' (mean anomaly) at 25 Oct.
